instructions: Start with the relish. In a small pot over medium-low, stir 1/2 cup vinegar, 1/2 cup sugar and a pinch of salt for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sugar dissolves. Take it off the heat and let it cool.
Meanwhile, cut the 2 cucumbers in half lengthwise and slice them thinly. Thinly slice the shallot. Put them both in a small serving bowl.
Thinly slice 2 of the chilies into a little dish for the table. Roughly chop the 2 tbsp peanuts.
Chop 1 tbsp of the cilantro and pick a small handful of leaves for the top. Squeeze 1 tbsp juice from half the lime.

Cut the 1 lb fish into chunks and put it in a food processor with 2 tbsp curry paste, 1 tbsp fish sauce, the egg, the chopped cilantro and the 1 tbsp lime juice. Blend for about 1 minute, scraping down the sides once, until it's a smooth, sticky paste.
Scrape the paste into a bowl. Slice 6 of the green beans into thin rounds and stir them in with the 1/4 cup rice flour until there's no dry flour left.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into 12 patties about 1/2 inch thick, using about 1/4 cup for each.

Heat 4 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Lay in half the patties and cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is deep golden. Flip them and cook the other side for 2 minutes. They're done when they've puffed a little and feel springy when you press one.
Move them to a plate lined with paper towels. Add the other 2 tbsp oil and cook the second batch the same way.
Pour the cooled syrup over the cucumbers and shallot and scatter the peanuts on top.
Cut the other half of the lime into wedges.
Serve the fish cakes with the cilantro leaves on top, with the cucumber relish, lime wedges and sliced chilies on the side.
method_notes: All three grind white fish with red curry paste, egg and fish sauce into a sticky paste, stir in thin slices of green bean and fry small flat cakes until golden. RecipeTin Eats, the lead, blends it in a food processor with cilantro, lime juice and rice flour, shapes 12 patties from 1 lb and shallow fries them 2 minutes a side, serving them with sweet chilli sauce. Temple of Thai and ImportFood work the paste by hand, add kaffir lime leaves and fry in deeper oil, and both serve a cucumber relish of cucumber, shallot and chilli in a cooled vinegar and sugar syrup with crushed peanuts. This one follows the lead's cakes with 2 tbsp curry paste instead of 3 to keep them milder, and serves ImportFood's relish with the chilies on the side.
